doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How big is his body of compositions
summary: Walton estimates around two hundred recorded compositions, notes his catalog took a full page in the Playboy Jazz Festival program.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How big is your body of work – compositions?

Uh, I'd have to research that one. It's not small though. I mean uh, it's not, there are people who have done more, of course. I'm not up with Ellington with the two thousand plus compositions recorded, but I might be up to two hundred, which is uh, I'll settle for that for the moment. But uh, that's a good question. I saw uh a list of uh my works in the program of the Playboy Jazz Festival just uh – what month was that? – either August or September. And it just happened to show uh, uh, uh, my stuff took up a whole page. I was surprised. I had forgotten a lot of these things that I had recorded. And they had 'em all in there, more than anybody else on the program. But I mean uh, that wasn't necessarily accurate that I'd done more than anybody else, but … there were people on there like George Benson, so one of his pieces might uh have uh, uh, uh gone at a revenue of all of mine, you know. [chuckles] So, that's the way that works uh, it's uh, uh a matter of quantity not quality.
